title: Commission a walk-in cold-storage thermostat
objective: Select and validate the simplest discrete controller that maintains the qualified product-temperature band without short-cycling the compressor.
physicalPurpose: Protect stored product and compressor cycling through an explainable thermostat, equipment-owned restart permission, and tested abnormal behavior.

simplifications: Room air and stored product are represented by one well-mixed thermal state.
The model omits refrigerant pressures, defrost, humidity, electrical starting current, product-core temperature, and compressor wear.
The running feedback exactly follows the simulator command; physical starter and protection timing require separate evidence.
All results are Simulation evidence and do not establish food safety or authorize a physical compressor.

baseline.limitation: A single switching threshold reacts repeatedly to qualified measurement noise near the boundary.

change.decision: Compare single-threshold, hysteresis-only, and hysteresis-plus-dwell behavior under equivalent conditions, then select the simplest candidate satisfying product-band, cycling, restart, quality, and recovery requirements.

disturbances: Apply the same seeded 0.03 degC measurement-noise record to all candidates.
Raise the no-cooling equilibrium from 4 to 6 degC from 60 through 90 seconds to represent an open door.
Restart the controller at 100 seconds with starter readiness false for 5 seconds.
Invalidate temperature quality from 110 through 112 seconds, acknowledge in manual, recover automatic operation, and test manual mode from 120 through 123 seconds.

acceptance.window: normal automatic completed intervals before controller restart
normal automatic completed intervals before controller restart

abortPredicates: Temperature, timing, threshold, or dwell input is nonfinite or outside its declared range.
The applied command is neither 0 nor 100 percent.
The selected candidate violates a completed 5 second minimum interval outside a declared safety or manual interruption.
A nonzero command occurs with invalid temperature quality, starter not ready, or manual mode.
Simulation evidence is presented as food-safety, compressor-endurance, electrical, refrigeration, or physical commissioning evidence.
safety.restorationMode: Command 0%, establish valid temperature quality, acknowledge in manual, wait for equipment-owned starter readiness, then explicitly re-enter automatic mode.
safety.physicalApprovalRole: authorised refrigeration controls engineer with food-safety, electrical, mechanical, operations and equipment owners
simulationOnlyRestrictions: Do not start or stop a physical compressor from this capstone.
The simplified room-air response is not stored-product core-temperature evidence.
Physical commissioning requires reviewed refrigeration capacity, defrost, pressure, starter, electrical, alarm, food-safety, rollback, and approval evidence.

video.viewerOutcome: Commission and defend a complete cold-storage thermostat without being told the winning settings in advance.

learning.context: A walk-in food cold-storage room uses a discrete compressor, qualified air-temperature measurement, equipment-owned starter readiness, and a 1 to 3 degC product band around a 2 degC setpoint.
learning.reason: The earlier cold-room lessons exposed observation failure, single-threshold chatter, and the value of hysteresis and dwell; the capstone now requires an independent choice from requirements and equivalent evidence.
theory: Setpoint and process value define the temperature objective, while requested compressor demand and measured running feedback distinguish controller intent from applied equipment state.
Hysteresis separates the switch-on and switch-off boundaries so small measurement changes do not reverse state.
Minimum on and off times constrain completed applied-state intervals, while starter readiness owns physical restart permission.
A control threshold initiates ordinary action; a safety limit aborts the experiment and has a different owner.
learning.workedPrediction: Derive 2.5 and 1.5 degC thresholds from a 1.0 degC symmetric hysteresis about 2.0 degC, retain 0.5 degC static product-limit margin, and predict every ordinary completed on/off interval will be at least 5.0 seconds.
practicalPreparation: Record product limits, one-sided discrete actuator behavior, quality, starter readiness, sample interval, seed, door event, candidate settings, measure windows, aborts and Simulation label.
Predict which candidate will first satisfy both temperature and compressor-cycling requirements without viewing results.
learning.baseline: Run zero hysteresis and zero dwell against the fixed noise record and retain its measured applied-state transitions.
learning.change: Run hysteresis-only and hysteresis-plus-dwell candidates with all other conditions identical, then select the simplest eligible design.
learning.comparison: Classify candidate eligibility before comparing product-band time, temperature extremes, measured transitions, completed on/off durations and ineligible command count.
learning.validation: Validate the selected design through the door event, repeatability, controller restart, equipment-owned starter lockout, invalid-quality latch, manual safe state and explicit automatic recovery.
learning.explanation: Trace each temperature crossing into requested cooling, dwell and interlock decisions, applied compressor state, thermal response and recovery; explain why continuous control adds no authority to this installed actuator.
learning.transfer: Carry the same independent commissioning discipline into Lesson 77, where a continuously modulated water heater requires model, controller-structure and tuning decisions.
